localChanges: chore: update core-player, core-strategy-ai-client, civ1-player and simple-ai-client

log: CI failed to install: the yarn lock file couldn't resolve core-pending-effect ^0.1.2.

The criterion listed every other mandatory action, so each `Player.actions()` cost two full passes over the player's `Action` rules. It now asks `hasMandatoryActions()`, which core-player answers at the first rule offering one (civ-clone/web-renderer#314).
CI failed to install: the lock file pinned versions that no longer resolve against the current ranges (core-data-object ^0.1.15 was ETARGET).

`mandatoryAction()` and `hasMandatoryActions()` now walk the `Action` rules in order and stop at the first rule that offers a `MandatoryPlayerAction`, rather than building every action and filtering. An AI asks for its next action once per action it takes, and on a late-game save that was 277 ms a turn (civ-clone/web-renderer#314); it is now ~50 ms.

Each rule is processed before the next is validated, unlike `RuleRegistry.process`. Player `Action` rules only build `PlayerAction`s, so the action returned is the same one `mandatoryActions()[0]` would return. `actions()`, `mandatoryActions()` and `hiddenActions()` are unchanged.
It returns `undefined` when no rule offers a mandatory action, which the declared `MandatoryPlayerAction` hid from callers.

`takeTurn` called `hasMandatoryActions()` and then `mandatoryAction()` for every action, and each built the player's actions. It now calls `mandatoryAction()` once per action and stops on `undefined`, which core-player now declares (civ-clone/web-renderer#314).
The tests record only the client's own calls to the player's action methods, not the player's internal ones, so they hold whichever way core-player builds its answers.
test: a turn with no mandatory action ends at the first undefined

core-player now types `mandatoryAction()` as possibly `undefined` (civ-clone/web-renderer#314), which ts-mocha would reject when passed straight to `attempt`. Same loop as `StrategyAIClient.takeTurn`.
